description: A department head must finalize Taylor's annual performance rating and the accompanying feedback record after a difficult review cycle involving missed deliverables and changing priorities.

shared_context.S1: Taylor's annual performance review is due, and the draft currently flags missed deliverables as a concern.
shared_context.S2: Marisol has final authority over Taylor's performance rating and the written review record.
shared_context.S3: Several of Taylor's priorities changed during the review cycle, and the team is preparing its final calibration materials.
shared_context.S4: As part of the normal calibration meeting, Marisol conducts a round of input from the project lead, a peer colleague, and HR before finalizing the review.

PF1.text: Grant's project records show exactly six of Taylor's delayed deliverables were delayed because leadership reprioritized the work after Taylor had started it; Grant has not yet added this attribution to the calibration notes.

PF2.text: Nia directly observed exactly four occasions when Taylor identified a delivery risk early enough for the team to avoid an escalation; these examples have not been collected in Taylor's review packet.

PF3.text: Owen's confidential HR record confirms that Taylor worked under an approved 80 percent schedule for two months of the review cycle, so the goals for that period must be recalibrated to 80 percent of the standard capacity; the record has not been shared because the schedule arrangement is confidential.

acceptance_conditions: Taylor must receive a final rating of Meets Expectations, with exactly six delayed deliverables attributed to leadership reprioritization and exactly four early-risk interventions recorded.
The review record must attribute exactly six delayed deliverables to leadership reprioritization.
The review record must include exactly four early-risk interventions observed by a peer.
The review goals must be recalibrated for the approved reduced schedule.
The normalized capacity used for the recalibrated goals must be exactly 80 percent.
A commitment to update Taylor's performance review record must be logged.

content_checks.C1: decisions['reprioritized_delays_recorded'] == 6 and decisions['risk_interventions_recorded'] == 4 and ('Meets Expectations' in decisions['final_rating'] or 'meets expectations' in decisions['final_rating'] or 'revised upward' in decisions['final_rating'] or 'rating should reflect' in decisions['final_rating'])
content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'documentation' or c['type'] == 'documentation_update' or c['type'] == 'update_review_record' or c['type'] == 'draft_revision' or c['type'] == 'review_revision' for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: Knowing that exactly six delayed deliverables followed leadership reprioritization changes the rating to Meets Expectations and sets the attribution count to exactly 6.
Nia's firsthand account changes the rating to Meets Expectations and requires recording exactly 4 early-risk interventions.
The approved 80 percent schedule changes the goal-setting decision to recalibration with a normalized capacity of exactly 80 percent.
